utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is case number TT-98-34-T, the Prosecutor versus Naletilic and Martinovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Good morning, everybody. We are sorry we are late for about five minutes because of the technical problems. So, Mr. Prosecutor, are you ready for your next witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Yes, good morning, Mr. President, and Your Honours. We are prepared to call the next witness, who has requested protective measures. He has requested to use a pseudonym and to have face distortion while he testifies. The witness is currently a resident of Bosnia-Herzegovina, and so I don't expect there will be any objection from the Defence for the protective measures.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Are there any objections from Defence counsel?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honour. No, we have no objections.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honours. Our Defence also has no objections.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: So your request is granted.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. So if the witness could be brought in. While that's happening, perhaps I could inform the Trial Chamber of what we view as being the relevant parts of the indictment that will be touched upon by this witness's testimony. The main thrust, if I can say generally, will be the events which occurred in Sovici beginning on the 17th of April, 1993. The witness will give evidence relevant to paragraphs 7 and 11, which is the Background part of the indictment; paragraphs 14 through 17, relating to the superior responsibility of both of the accused; paragraphs 18 through 21 which relate to the existence of an international armed conflict and the existence of a wide-spread or systematic campaign for purposes of Articles 2 and 5 of the Statute. The witness's evidence will be relevant to paragraphs 25, 27 through 30, 32, and 34, which are all found in count 1, the persecution count, relating to the Sovici attack, prisoners at Ljubuski, the Heliodrom, and forced labour. The evidence will also be relevant to paragraphs 36 through 40, counts 2 through 8, regarding the use of prisoners for forced labour; and finally, Mr. President, the evidence will be relevant to paragraphs 45 and 50, counts 11 and 12 relating to beatings and mistreatment as cruel treatment and willfully causing great suffering or serious bodily injury. I should also add, Mr. President, that because of the position of this witness, it may be necessary to go into private session for a significant part of his testimony, the earlier part of it. But I think that as we get into that, I will alert the Trial Chamber.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Good morning, Witness.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Would you please make the solemn declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: You may sit down.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Witness, good morning.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Can you hear me all right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: I can hear you well.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Witness, I can inform you that the Trial Chamber has granted the protective measures that you have requested. So during your testimony, we will not be referring to you by your name, rather we're going to be calling you Witness Y, and I have a sheet of paper which I would like for you to look at and to tell us whether on this piece of paper you see your name and your date of birth, and I'm also going to ask you if this paper correctly indicates what was your position in April of 1993.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: Yes, this is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: We're going to wait just a moment until the others look at the paper, and then we'll begin your testimony. So, Witness, let me remind you that while you're testifying, try to keep in mind that you have protective measures so that you should not identify yourself or other members of your family or give information which might disclose your identity. Witness Y, let me ask you first, is your national or ethnic background Bosnian Muslim?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And did you -- were you born in the village of Sovici and did you live there all of your life until 1988?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: I was born in Sovici, and between 1988 and 1992, I lived in Mostar.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: During the period that you lived in Mostar, did you return to Sovici occasionally?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: For the most part, every week because my mother lived there.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And then in 1992, did you return to Sovici and continue living there until April of 1993?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: On 4th April, 1992, I came to Sovici to visit my mother, and it was Bajram, which is a Muslim holiday, and after that, I did not go back to Mostar.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Mr. President, with the assistance of the usher, I would like to give the witness an exhibit. It's a new exhibit which has been marked as Exhibit 3.3. It's a map. I think copies have already been distributed. Put it on the desk for now.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Witness, before we start hearing your story of what happened to you, I would like to ask you some questions generally about the village of Sovici as of April of 1993. Okay?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: In April of 1993, that is until the 17th of April, 1993, the atmosphere was rather good. There were no problems.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Let me ask you if you know approximately how many people lived in the village, and what was the ethnic or national background of the people living there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: Sovici had a little over 800 population. It's mixed Muslim and Croats. In Sovici, the majority was Muslim, predominantly, and Doljani had a predominantly Croat population, and Doljani was larger than Sovici.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: The village of Sovici, was it divided or did it fall into a smaller number of hamlets?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: It consisted of several small hamlets, for instance Donja Mahala, Srednja Mahala, Gornja Mahala, like lower, middle, upper middle Mahala.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Gornja Mahala being the upper part, Donja Mahala being the lower part, Srednja Mahala being the middle part. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Now, can you tell us, if you know, again, generally the ethnic composition of these hamlets?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: Donja Mahala was mixed, Muslims and Croats. The was purely Croatian, and Gornja Mahala was pure Muslim, but there was also a hamlet called Cilici which was mixed Croats and Muslims.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Just for the record, I think, because we are not picking up some of these words in the English transcript, I think, if I may, Gornja being spelled G-O-R-N-J-A, Srednja Mahala, S-R-E-D-N-J-A, Mahala, M-A-H-A-L-A, and Donja Mahala, D-O-N-J-A Mahala.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I think you have to ask the witness whether your spelling is correct or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Very well, Mr. President, I will do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Witness, I have just spelled the names of the hamlets which you have described. Is that spelling correct? Do you see the names now spelled correctly on the transcript in front of you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Now, Witness, I'm going to ask the usher to give you a red pen. And if you can, on the map, if you could show us just by circling --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I saw Mr. Seric is standing.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My apologies. A technical question. The witness did not have a transcript in front of him when he confirmed the spelling, so the transcript was actually not showing on his monitor.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: So, Mr. Stringer, will you please do it once again, and the usher will check whether the...

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Witness, let me just ask you, you said Gornja Mahala. Can you please spell that.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: G-O-R-N-J-A M-A-H-A-L-A.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Can you spell Srednja.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: S-R-E-D-N-J-A M-A-H-A-L-A.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And, finally, Donja Mahala, can you spell that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: D-O-N-J-A M-A-H-A-L-A.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, Witness, with the red pen, if you could just make a circle around these three places, particularly if they correspond to locations on the map.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Okay, now I'm going to ask first to put that on the ELMO. That way, everyone can see the places the witness has marked. Okay, that's fine. Thank you. Now, Witness Y, I see that you have circled, placed three circles on this map. One circle around the letter G. What place is that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: This is Gornja Mahala, this is Srednja Mahala, and this is Donja Mahala.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: So the letters on the map appear to correspond to the names you've just given us.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Mr. President, at this time I would like to ask that the witness be shown Exhibit Number 6.3, which is a photograph. I think the ELMO is okay. Place it on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Okay, now, Witness, looking at this photograph, if you can, again, first using pointer, show us the location, if it's on this photo, the area of Gornja Mahala.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: This is Gornja Mahala.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And generally, what was the ethnic composition of that part of the village?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: Here Muslims; and here Muslims; and in this area, it was mixed, Muslims and Croats.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Okay. Taking the red pen again, could you just put a circle around the area that you call Gornja Mahala.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Thank you. Well, you mentioned -- well, looking at the photograph, do you see any other hamlets on the photograph which you've mentioned?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: I see Srednja Mahala.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And again, what was the ethnic composition of Srednja Mahala?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: Croats populated Srednja Mahala.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Again, taking the pen - and it might be better to give the witness a different pen so it makes a better mark on the photo - I'll ask you to place a circle around the area you call Srednja Mahala.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Okay, in that circle somewhere, if you could just place the letters "SM" for Srednja Mahala. And then in the other circle, the letters "GM" for Gornja Mahala.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Mr. President, with your permission, at this time I would like to ask the technical people to play Exhibit Number 4, it's one of the very short video clips which the Trial Chamber saw at the beginning of the trial, which might assist, again, in just orientating in respect of Sovici.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: I don't know if we're able to do this or not. I think it's coming.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Touch the Video button. You should be able to see it. Does everyone see it?

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Witness, do you see the videotape on your screen?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Can you tell us what area we're looking at right now.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: This is Gornja Mahala, Upper Mahala. The mosque destroyed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Now, what area do we see now?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: Now we see Srednja, Middle Mahala, and just a few -- this is the Middle Mahala, Srednja Mahala, but we just saw a couple of bricks which belong to the Donja or Lower Mahala.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Mr. President, I don't think we have a way to mark the videotape, but I think that it's in evidence and the Trial Chamber should be able to link it to the photograph which has been circled.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Now, Witness Y, I would like to now ask you to look at Exhibit 8.2, which is a different photograph. Let me ask you first, are you aware of a hamlet or an area in Sovici called Junuzovic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: I am, and that's where it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Now, you are pointing to the extreme right-hand side of the photograph. Could I ask you just to circle that place you're pointing to and place a "J" there for Junuzovic.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Now, just looking at this photograph, off to the left there is a road. Can you tell us what road that is?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: It connects Sovici, Doljani, and then goes on to Jablanica.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Now, I'm going to ask you now to look at Exhibit 8.8, which is a different photograph. Now, Witness Y, do you know this place?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And what was this place?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: Next to the fish pond here was the HVO command.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Now, going back to the map, which is Exhibit 3.3, I'd like to ask you to make a couple of marks on the map. Using the red pen again, Witness Y, if you could just take a moment to look at the map and tell us, if you can, generally speaking, the location of that place called Junuzovic.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: Junuzovici.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Yes. I see you've made a circle. Just underneath the circle, can you place a "J" for Junuzovic.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Okay, again on the map, if you can, can you mark the location of this place that you said was an HVO base.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Just underneath that mark, can you place the letters "HVO."

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Okay, and now with the assistance of the usher, I would like the map to be placed on the ELMO so everyone can see where you've made these marks. Using the pointer, Witness Y, can you tell us the place that you marked as the Junuzovic location.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And then can you also show us what you've marked as the location of the HVO base.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Just in terms of scale, and for Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. the Trial Chamber, Mr. President, if you look at the bottom of the map, you'll see that the scale is 1 centimetre for 500 metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: But Witness Y, let me ask you if you could tell us, just roughly, the distance between this HVO base and Donja Mahala going along the main road.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: Three kilometres.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Now, while we're looking at the map, there's another road which appears on the map and which also appeared in the photograph that contained the Junuzovici houses. Is there another road that goes through Junuzovic toward a place called Risovac?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Can you, just using the pointer, show us where that road is located on this map.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Okay, now, is there also a different road that goes to Risovac?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: There is.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. We'll come back to that. Okay, you can set the pointer down, and we can set the map aside for now. Witness Y, were you in Sovici on the 15th of April, 1993?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: I was, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: What happened on that day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: On the 15th of April, '93, in the afternoon hours, the shelling of the village of Risovac began -- I mean Jablanica.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: You say there was shelling in Jablanica.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And do you know where the shelling was coming from?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: From Risovac, from Junuzovici houses where the heavy artillery had been put in place.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Did you see the place Risovac on the map that you were just looking at?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And what was the situation in Sovici, then, on the 15th, while Jablanica was being shelled?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: Tense, naturally; an expectation of the shelling of Sovici, however, Sovici was not shelled on the 15th of April, 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Then, moving ahead to the 17th of April, 1993, what happened on that day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: On the 17th of April, '93, in the morning, at 8:00, the shelling of the village of Sovici began, by and large the upper part, that is Gornja Mahala.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Where were you when the shelling started?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: When the shelling started, I was at home, the house that I was born in. And then I went to the command post, not far from my house, but I could not establish communication with my superior command so that I went back and then moved to a place called Kamen

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Why were you unable to establish contact with the others?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: Because the power was cut on the 15th of April, '93.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Do you know or were you able to tell where the shelling was coming from at that time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: From all sides, from all around Sovici. But chiefly from Risovac.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Was all of Sovici targeted by the shelling?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: All parts of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: What did the civilian population do when the shelling started?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: Well, by and large, those who had some cellars went to cellars; who didn't, fled to other people's cellars.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Can you give us an idea of the intensity of the shelling; how frequently were shells landing in the village?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: Every second, there would be one, I mean.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: How long did this shelling last?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: From 8.00 in the morning until quarter to 5.00 in the afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Mr. President, at this time I think it's necessary to go into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: We'll go to private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, we are now in the open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: When you were in Ljubuski, did you receive any information about what was happening or what had happened in Sovici after you left?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: Yes, two days later, that is on the 21st of April, '93, some soldiers came who wanted to kill us. And they said that their commander Cikota had been killed and therefore they had come to slay us all, and Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. that our whole village had been set on fire. And meanwhile, a man turned up who prevented them from shooting us all. I was beaten until I fainted, and I still have scars on my head -- rather, a depression on my head as a result of that beating.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Now, after 47 days, were you and other prisoners taken to a different place?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: After 47 days, they came and said 105 prisoners should go to work, and I was one of them. And I believed what they said, because in front of the prison, I saw two UN vehicles, and I thought they were going to take us for exchange --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction, in the previous sentence, it should be "exchange," not "work."

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: But they put us there, took us to Heliodrom, said we were late for the exchange and that we would have to wait for the next day.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Okay. Witness Y, just so the record is clear, did you say that they came and told us that 105 prisoners were going to be exchanged?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: Yes, yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: So then, you arrived at the Heliodrom, and how long or ultimately, eventually, what's the date that you were released from the Heliodrom?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: 1st of March, '94.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Now, during the time that you were in the Heliodrom, where were you held?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: When we arrived at Heliodrom, I spent all the time in one building, but at first I was on an upper floor for a period of time. And then they transferred me to the prison, and then from the prison, they moved me several times to different solitary confinement cells, and then once again back to the room where I stayed until the exchange.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: I would like to ask that the witness be shown Exhibits 20.2, 20.11, two photographs.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Witness, if you could look at these photographs, please, tell us if you see the place where you were held when you were at the Heliodrom.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Okay. And this is Exhibit Number 20.2. Could you please place a circle around that building with the pen.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Okay. And then just above that circle, if you could place a letter "Y" because you are Witness Y.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Okay, and looking at the other photograph, again, do you see the same building in that photograph?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Can you place a circle around that building, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Could you please, again, place the letter "Y" above that circle.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, I'm not sure, you said letter Y --

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: It looks a bit different than what I would make, Mr. President. Perhaps I could just ask the witness to make a different mark, perhaps a number "1" on that circle, just a number "1."

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Then going back, could you also please place a number "1" by the other photograph.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Mr. President, I think these photos will get their own exhibit number as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Now, Witness, you said that when you first arrived at the Heliodrom, I believe you said that you were in a place with other prisoners. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Can you -- and what building was that place? Is that the building that you were just marking on the photographs?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Can you describe the conditions there, this first part of the building in which you were held?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: There were two rooms, one next to another. One was large. When we first arrived, we were all placed there. And at first, it wasn't so bad. Half of the room was -- had some kind of metal beds so that the ones who were weak could spend the night there. Because they were saying every day that there would be an exchange so, from day to day, we were expecting this exchange the next day.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And you indicated that at some point, then, you were placed in a different location.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: Then I was taken from that room to the basement, to a room next to the staircase, where people passed when they went to get their meals. That room was made entirely of concrete with only an iron door, and that was a solid door with no opening of any kind on it, and when it closed there was no-one, no opening, nothing…

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: How long, if you remember, did you stay with the others in the big room upstairs?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: When I first arrived, well, I was there for a while, maybe a month and a half up there. And then I was transferred downstairs to the prison cell.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And please describe for us the conditions in the second room that you were transferred to.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: Very poor. I had nothing there except for a pail that I used, a bucket that I used for a toilet.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Was there any lighting in the room?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Was any light able to come into the room from outside?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: So it was completely dark in this room?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: 100 percent.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: How long did you remain in this room?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: About 40 days in that room.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Can you describe for us generally the treatment that you received while you were being held in that room?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: For the most part, I was always beaten. I had to step out in the hallway.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: There was a shift that I knew would always beat me when they were on duty unless I had to work. And if I was beaten so badly I couldn't move, then they would leave me alone for a couple of days until I recovered enough.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Were you able to wash yourself while you were in this cell?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Did anyone assist you in washing in any way?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: No. Only when they would beat me up, when I fainted, then they would bring in a hose, they would hose me down, and then they would leave me like that in that puddle.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Do you know what unit these guards belonged to?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: They always said that we were Tuta's prisoners, and that they belonged to Tuta.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: The guards themselves, did they belong to any particular HVO units, the guards in the Heliodrom?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: No, they only had the insignia as the military police do, the metal ones where it said military police.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: During the time that you were held at the Heliodrom, were you ever taken out to perform labour?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: Yes, all the others were. They went to work nonstop. I only went four times, four times it was that I left the facility.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Did you ever go into Mostar?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: One occasion I went to Mostar to the Health Centre.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: I'll ask the witness be shown Exhibit 14.5, which is a photograph.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Now, Witness Y, let me ask you, the time that you were taken to what you call the Health Centre, at what stage of your detention at the Heliodrom did this occur?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: Well, I was upstairs with all the other prisoners, before I was taken downstairs to the cell.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Now, looking at this photograph, 14.5, are you able to recognise any place that you worked at?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: Yes, I can. This here.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And can you just take a pencil and put a circle around that area that you've just pointed to.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: You mentioned the Health Centre. Why did you say the Health Centre?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: Because before the war, a hospital was there, and it was called the Health Centre.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Can you place a number "1" by the circle that you've just made, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Witness Y, can you tell us, then, what happened on the day that you were taken to this location to work?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: They put us in cars, took us to Rondo, and then on foot we were brought through this area, and when we were brought there, we were made to sit down against a wall of this building. And several people in uniform meanwhile arrived. One of them ordered us to lie behind the wall. And then they started shooting bursts of fire, I guess over us. Then some hand grenades were hurled. One started moaning and he -- I knew him from before. His name was Tsotsa. They all started beating him. One of them came back and asked us who was the strongest among us, and one young man said that he was, and then he said anybody else? Nobody else responded, and he designated one other soldier, and he said that the two of you tried to lift him. And they tried, and then he said fine, now you have a job to do.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: You mentioned that you were sitting against the wall of a building and shooting was taking place. Is that in the location that you just marked on the photograph with the circle?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: There's a concrete wall there, behind this building. It's paved with concrete, and then there is a wall, and we were there.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Do you know or did you learn the identity of any of the persons who were beating this person you've called Tsotsa?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: The one who was giving orders turned around and asked one of the prisoners, "How come you're here?" And he said, "You see, Stela, I was at Capljina, and went to my mother's at Sovici. This is how I got stuck," and this is how I knew that this was Stela.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: You mentioned that two persons were selected and they had a job to do. What was their job?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: The one who later introduced himself as Stela said that one of our prisoners was -- had tried to escape, but he was killed in the process, and they needed to bring his body back from this intersection here. The two of them went, indeed, and brought back the body.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Was there anyone in your group who knew this person Stela?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: There was a name called Hasib Lulic who later told me that he and Stela were both serving time in the corrections centre in Zenica before the war.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Did you and the others then leave this location and move to a different location?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: For the most part, they moved us next to this kindergarten. We were to dig the trenches and move sand bags, and we had to do this until the dark.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And then where did you go next?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: Then they took us back to Rondo and in front of that building, they told us to sit down and look down. And this man was again being beaten, and then he was taken to the cellar of the building. Then they brought him back. They went in to beat him. They brought him back and they put him on the truck and we went away.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: You mentioned the Rondo. What is this place that you were taken to at the Rondo?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: It was in front of a building, and the people who had brought us there told us that this was Stela's command post.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Did you see who was beating this man when you were in the area of the Rondo?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: While they were beating him outside, most of those who were around were beating him, Stela himself and all the others. And after they brought him -- after they took him down to the basement, I could only hear his screams and moans.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: That man that you saw in Sovici who introduced himself as Mladen Naletilic, Tuta, did you ever see him again after the 18th of April, 1993?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: Yes, I saw him twice at the Heliodrom in Mostar.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Would you please tell us about each of those occasions when you saw him.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: When I first transferred from Ljubuski to Heliodrom, we were in a room whose windows looked to the area in front of the building. And an Audi 100 model came; it was white. And Tuta came out and entered the building, but he did not enter the room in which I was staying at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Did you see Tuta again when you were at the Heliodrom?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: The second time was when I was in a prison cell. The police opened the door, and I was ordered to introduce myself to Tuta. I did. And he said that the conditions that I was in were good compared to what I deserved for what I had done.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Can you describe the prison cell that you were being held in at that time.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: You come down the staircase from the upper floor, and then you go straight, and then you arrived in the area where the cell was. It was all concrete, and it had an iron door, or metal door.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Is this the same cell that you described earlier that was -- had no light in it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And after then you saw Tuta, what took place?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: They went back, and five minutes later, the military policeman came, ordered me to come out in front of the cell. I did. Then they started beating me with all kinds of things. There were all kinds of things that they were -- implements, and they started beating me, and I fell down and blood was dripping on the floor. And one of those who beat me ordered me to lick the blood because no balija blood should remain on Croatian soil, he said.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Witness Y, did you lose any weight during the ten months that you were held at Ljubuski and at the Heliodrom?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: 40 kilograms.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Witness, at this time, I'm going to ask you to look around the courtroom. Tell us if you recognise anyone present whom you've testified about today.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: I recognise Mladen Naletilic, Tuta. Stela is a little different. When I saw him, he had no hair. He had his head shaved, and Tuta had different glasses. The frame was different. They were round. And his beard is now grey. It was not at that time. And he has less hair than before.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Witness Y, for the record, could you just tell us where these -- first of all, starting with Mr. Naletilic, can you tell us for the record where he is located in the courtroom? Can you describe his position and perhaps how he is dressed.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: He is wearing glasses. He is wearing a suit, white shirt, longish hair.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: What about the tie?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: Yes, a tie. From what I can see here, it's red and blue, blue with red dots.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And then the person you've identified as "Stela," can you tell us where he is seated and how he is dressed. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: He is also wearing a suit, a blue shirt, and a blue tie, receding hair. I think that they also recognise me.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Mr. President, no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Any documents you are going to tender into evidence?

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I am going to tender several. I can do it now or later. Several of them are already in evidence, but there are a couple of new ones.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Maybe at the end of the re-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Any cross-examinations.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. And I will conduct the cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Krsnik, before you start, there are two things I would like to remind you. The first one is you and the witness are speaking the same language, so do please make a pause after each question. The second one is that this witness gave most of the part of his testimony in private session. If your question concerns that part, we'll go into the private session, too. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Your Honour. I will definitely keep your words in mind.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Witness. I am the Defence counsel for the accused Naletilic, and I will ask some questions of you. I would like to ask you to please carefully listen to them and give us as short answers as you can, because the questions will be framed that way so that we would not waste any time unnecessarily.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, well, Mr. Krsnik, could we go into the private session. We'll go to the private session.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You said infantry weapons.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: [No verbal response]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Are PAMs, that is, anti-aircraft mortars and mortars, are they part of infantry weaponry?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: So you had both PAM, the anti-aircraft machine-guns, and mortars?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: We had two mortars, .62 millimetres, and one anti-aircraft, 13.72 millimetres.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And where were they positioned?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: The mortars and the PAMs, the anti-aircraft, they were at Duga Gruda, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: So the PAM was at Duga Gruda, and the mortars?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: One was in the lower part of Sovici, in Donja Mahala, and the other one in at the upper part of Sovici.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And when you were issued with it, it was in case of a Serb attack? You needed it to fight the Serbs, is it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: We had to have them as a unit. If we went to Igman or whatever, we needed to have this accompany us as a kind of infantry weapons.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The witness nods.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And tell me, where is it that you went, this Sovici Battalion, where else did you go except Sovici?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: Hadzici.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: When was that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: The 1st of June, '92 until the 10th of June '92.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: But you said that at times it was the TO, so the Croats went with you, didn't they?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: No, they didn't go with us even then.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: What kind of weapons did your soldiers have? I mean the BH army in Sovici?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: By and large, M-48 rifles, semi-automatic, and a few automatic rifles.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Tell me, you say M-48 rifles. We are not military experts. Is that a bad gun? What's wrong with it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: I didn't say it was bad. That's what the rifle is called. It came from the former Yugoslav army.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: Well, I wouldn't be able to tell you to the last man, but I should say 250 to 30 [sic] were inhabitants of Sovici, in Sovici.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Yes, yes, yes, I'm asking you about Sovici. We shall later on move to some statements that you gave. I remember you making some Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. statements apart from this one in the Court today. Did anyone interview you about the events in Sovici?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: Well, earlier, yes, in Bosnia-Herzegovina only.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And nobody else ever interviewed you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Did you talk with the representatives of this Tribunal?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: No. It was mostly people from Bosnia-Herzegovina who were representing somebody, saying we should give those statements. Well, there were some officials, but I don't know any one of them so I cannot say really, but they were all from Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: If I understand you well, you gave statements only to people from Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And they were the ones who brought some foreigners to you and those foreigners listened to you or what? I don't understand.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: Nothing. I gave those statements. I think I was called two or three times to those same people from Bosnia-Herzegovina, they wanted to talk to me, whether I would testify about this and then I said I would. And then there was somebody, I don't know who, but there was somebody from the international community or perhaps even from here. I wouldn't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And tell me, who is it in Bosnia-Herzegovina who called you, invited you that you give a statement? Who are those people?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: Well, they were mostly people from state security.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: When you say "state security," do you mean the secret police, do you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And that secret police, then, brought those foreigners when they interviewed you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Do you remember those statements that you gave?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: In one of those statements, you said that there were not more than 200, that is, there were 200 Croats in Sovici. Today you say 250, 300 inhabitants. I'm asking you about the inhabitants, about the residents of Sovici.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: I don't remember ever saying the exact 200, but I said there were twice as many Muslims as Croats, and in Doljani --

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: No, no, no, let's leave Doljani alone. We will get to Doljani. I am asking you about Sovici. Right, now tell me, please, and what was the Muslim population or the Bosnian population, whatever, we can call them Bosnians or Muslims, please don't get me wrong. Say how many Muslim residents were there in Sovici?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: About four to five hundred.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Do you remember the statement that you gave - I don't know to whom - on the 29th of April, 1997?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Do you remember signing that statement?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And whenever you gave those statements, you told the truth, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And in that statement, you said that in the village of Sovici, which was made of several hamlets, there were 612 Muslims and around 200 Croats, and this is three times as many Muslims as are Croats. You gave the exact figure. And that was in '97.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: Well, if I said so and signed it, then that must be it. Then it must be correct. Then that is how it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Mm-hmm. And will you please tell me if members of the BH army from either villages or towns came to your village?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: No, they didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Never, not a single member of the BH army outside Sovici came to your place?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: Never, not one member of the BH army from anywhere else came to Sovici.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Not even prior to the 17th to help you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Very well. Now, you still owe me a question, I believe we still have one question unresolved. Those positions in '93, you manned them throughout, I mean Mackovic, Gruda, Pasje Stijene, Povrsak. The BH army holds those positions, doesn't it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: Mackovic, Duga Gruda, and Povrsak.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Right, right. These are lines against whom in 1993, March, April?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: Against the one who attacks us.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And from those three elevations or hills, whatever you care to call them, why don't you control the whole Sovici valley and Blidinje valley from those positions?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: No, no, no, we do not have that kind of armament to control them.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Very well. Tell me what is the PAMs range?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: 5.000 metres, as far as I know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And tell me, please, how far is Mackovic or Gruda from Sovicka Vrata?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: Well, four or five hundred metres as the crow flies, 500 metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Now, would you be so kind as to tell us the Blidinje valley, say at Zenica or Siroki Dolac, how far is that from Mackovic and Gruda?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: Three or 4 kilometres.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And now, tell me, please, what is the range of the .60 millimetre mortar?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: Well, about a thousand metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: You said that your command was at a place called Kamen.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: If I am correct, you even drew it on that photograph.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: Then, sir, you misunderstood me.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Yes, that is possible. I'm sorry then.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: I said that I went to the command at Begici, which is in the upper part of Sovici, and when I couldn't establish contact, it is then that I went to the position at Kamen.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Fine, fine, I think I got your meaning. All I wanted was to ask you about that Kamen. Is that an elevation?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Is it exactly above Croat houses, that is, the Srednja Mahala?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: Between the Gornja and Srednja Mahala, there is a --

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Yes, I know, I know, I know. Now, will you please be so kind to answer me. This place, Kamen, is it exactly on an elevation above Croat houses? Yes or no, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Did you have any protection around that command, I mean some trenches, some machine-gun nests or something like that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: We didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And Srednja Mahala, tell me, was it protected by trenches on the Sovicka Vrata side?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: Yes, it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Those were the BH army positions, weren't they?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Fine. Now, tell me, you were explaining that there was the Gornja, Srednja, Donja Mahala. Could you please tell us how many hamlets are there along that line?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: Quite a number of them. You want me to list them all?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Yes, will you please be so kind if it is not too much trouble, but do it slowly for the record. How many hamlets and if you can tell us also which were Muslim and which were Muslim [sic], thank you very much. I would be most grateful to you, and I believe the Chamber would, too.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: In Gornja Mahala, you have -- let's make it easier; next to the mosque, Brajkovici. Then to the left, when you cross over a 100 metres off is Begici, and then Zivkovici. Above Zivkovici is Lucani, Skenderi, this is the Muslim people. Cilici, a mixed place, Muslims and Croats. Srednja Mahala, Croats. Mijici, Croats only. Dolac, mixed Muslims and Croats. Podrubina, Muslims. Raici, Croats. Junuzovici, Muslims. I believe I've listed them all.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Thank you very much indeed. And all these hamlets are scattered along the road, east and west of the road, if I can put it that way?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Only Srednja Mahala is right next to the road, if I saw it well.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: Well, Srednja and Gornja Mahala for the most part, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Now, if you could tell the Chamber, these hamlets, how far are they from the road as the crow flies, generally speaking? All those hamlets you just mentioned.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: Raici, 200 metres. Junuzovici, 500 metres. Mijici, next to the road. Dolac, 300 metres. Podgradina, 500 metres. In other words, Kula, I forgot it last time, Kula is right next to the road, houses on both sides of the road. Srednja Mahala is next to the road, above the road. Donja Mahala is, for the most part, that is, Gornja Mahala, Brajkovici Skenderi and so on and so forth. Lucani is a hundred metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Fine, fine, thank you. We needed to get a picture because, you know, we haven't been there so that I simply wanted to get the -- as objective a picture as possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is 1.00. Everybody is warning me, and I have finished already with the larger part of my questions. I will continue after the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. We will adjourn until 1.30 [sic]. --- Luncheon recess taken at 1.00 p.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Krsnik, please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Witness, would you please be so kind and tell me, what elevations are Mackovic, Gruda, and Povrsak? What is their elevation above sea level?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: About 1.000 metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Now, please tell me if there is any fighting going on there, infantry battles, would that have threatened the population of Sovici, to leave Doljani outside of that for now?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: Let me please explain what the defence lines were in Sovici, in the village of Sovici.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Please let me alert you to the questions. Mackovica, Gruda, Povrsak, I am referring to those elevations. If you have infantry operations there, any fighting going on there, would that have threatened the population of Sovici?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And Sovici are at what elevation, please?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: About 600 metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Can you now please tell us, how far is Risovac from Jablanica, what is the distance?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: 22 kilometres.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: I see. 22 kilometres, and how high is that mountain?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: I think that the elevation is 800 metres, but it's not a mountain, it's a plateau. It's a bowl.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Yes, I know that, but there is -- there are mountains around it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: Yes, there's Cvrsnica, and there's Vran on the other side.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: That's right. How high are they?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: I think that Vran is 1700 metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And Cvrsnica?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: A little bit less.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Today, when you gave your evidence to my learned colleague, you said that the artillery was firing all over Sovici and that shells were falling every second, as you put, from 8.00 in the morning until almost 5.00 in the afternoon. Is that what you said earlier today?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: I did a little math. That would have meant 28.000 shells having fallen?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: Perhaps even more.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Can you please tell me which houses were hit on that date, the 17th, which you could see when you came down that night?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: When I came down to the hamlet of Brajkovici.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Can you please give us the sort of overall number throughout Sovici?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: I had no time to review the situation throughout Sovici, but where I came -- I can only tell you about the place where I went to pick up the car.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: How many houses are there in Sovici altogether, if you know?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: About 100, 120 houses.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: You mean 100 total?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: No, Muslims.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And grand total?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: Two, three hundred. I don't know. I've never taken that count.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Can you now tell me about the mosque. Was this a mosque or was it a gazulhana, as Muslims say?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: This was a mosque, newly built, and minaret had not been built, so there was no minaret.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: So how can a person who doesn't know, know that it was a mosque?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: There was an old mosque there previously which -- and it was reconstructed and a new one was built.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Could I have known that this was a mosque if I went to Sovici?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: You could have.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: How could I have known?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: From the shape of the roof, from the entrance door, the door was from the north, and the structure looked like a mosque.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And those were the features that would have made me identify it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: Also, there was cemetery around it with headstones which we called basluci, so that would have also been a clue.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Let me take you back to the statements you gave, the one you gave on the 29th of April, '97. In it, you stated that at Obruc, you were approached by a man who you understood to be a commander. And that later on, another man arrived in a Patrol make of a car, with a hat on his head, who told you to take your family to Jablanica with you in the car and that the rest should go in a bus. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: Yes. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Did you shake hands when he approached?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And was the first man who you identified, was he a commander?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: He looked like a commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Now, please tell me, what were the insignia that they had on their sleeves, those men at Obruc?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: There were all kinds.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Now, tell me about that colonel who allegedly questioned you. What was his name again?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: Ivan Andabak.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please have the spelling that the witness used, which was "Anderbak."

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Witness, you keep repeating "Anderbak." We speak the same language, I could hear you well. Do you see that his name was Anderbak?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: That is how he introduced himself to me. This is what I stated in my statements.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Will you please spell it for me now.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: A-N-D-E-B-A-R-K.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: What kind of insignia was he -- did he have on his uniform?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: In the primary school, he used to sit --

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: No, no, no, that's not my question. What was the patch on his sleeve?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: I was too afraid to look so I couldn't see all the details.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Yes, I understand. But today, you placed him with a Convicts' Battalion.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: I said when they were coming out of the house where they were meeting, they had insignia --

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Who?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: Some of them had only HVO insignia.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Very well. Let's just deal with them. Those that you were just referring to, do you know some of their names?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: I know quite a few of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Will you please tell us their names, and please go slow for the record.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: Stipe Kopilas, Marko Rozic, Juka Groznica, Stipe Pole, Ivan Rogic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: They were wearing the Convicts' Battalion insignia?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: No, the HVO insignia.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Witness, a moment ago you just said that some had this insignia. What I am asking you -- what I was asking you whether you knew some of the men who had these Convicts' Battalion insignia?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: Mladen Naletilic, Tuta, Cikota, and the colonel.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Now, what did it look like, this emblem?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: On the sleeve you see it was circular, and it said "Convicts Battalion."

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Did it have anything else there in addition to the lettering?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: Yes, it had a checkerboard.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Was it a full checkerboard or how?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: I don't know. I never held it in my hand to see.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Yes, but you said a moment ago that you did not see that on Anderbak?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: I didn't see it, and in the primary school while he was questioning, he was sitting at a desk, wearing a sweater.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Now, tell me, you said that the person to whom you refer as "Tuta," that he addressed some older man. What was his name?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: Rafo Cvitkovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: He was also from Sovici?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: The people you listed a moment ago, were they all from the Mijat Tomic Battalion?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Today you said that this was the 3rd battalion -- the 3rd Battalion of what?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: I don't know. I only know that that is how it was called. That was its name.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Was this 3rd Battalion or this Mijat Tomic Battalion – did it belong to the same unit as your battalion? Let's say you were under a mountain brigade, were they a part of a brigade?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: No, not at Jablanica. That was the brigade. That was the brigade that existed in the Jablanica municipality. It was called – the 3rd Mijat Tomic Battalion. That was a brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Did you hear of a Herceg Stjepan brigade?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: I had heard about it but I don't know where it was or who was in it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And do you know what zone of responsibility was of that brigade or of the Mijat Tomic Battalion?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: I have no idea.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: The photograph that you were shown with a house and a fish pond, you said that that was the HVO command post. Was that the Mijat Tomic Battalion command post?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Could you please tell me, and now we're moving down to Doljani where this command post was, who held the checkpoints on route to Jablanica, on the Jablanica side, on the Doljani side?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: One checkpoint existed at the exit of Jablanica town, which was manned jointly by Croats and Muslims, by the civilian police.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Do you know how many troops were there in Jablanica, that is the AbiH members?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: As I said previously, about 1600.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Can you please tell me, were there not any special units active there, Zulfikar Ali Spago, called "Zuka" and others?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: No, not while I was there in that area.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And do you know who the president was and whose zone of responsibility Jablanica was?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: Nijaz Ivkovic.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter didn't catch the last name.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: What about Safet Cibo?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: Safet Cibo came to Jablanica maybe ten days before the conflict, supposedly to be the president of municipality there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, the interpreter said that he did not catch the last name. I think in this cross-examination, it involves a lot of names of places and people. You have to be very careful, and we have to slow down a little bit in your cross with these kind of names. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. I wasn't going to interrupt, and also I'm trying to stay focused because I'm running a high temperature, so if I miss something, I apologise. I'm not able to follow completely what's going on, and I thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: We mentioned Safet Cibo last, and I believe it was -- it is not in the transcript. Yes, your answer is not in the transcript.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: Yes, there was Safet Cibo, Dr. Safet Cibo.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: You said that he arrived just ten days before the conflict?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And then you said that he came to assume the post of the president of Konjic and Jablanica

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: Yes, he was told that he had come to become the president of the Konjic, Jablanica, Prozor area.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: He was appointed directly from Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: Most probably, but I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And he replaced a legally appointed leadership which was in place until then?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: I don't know what happened then

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: On the eve of the conflict in Sovici, that there was a terrible massacre of Croats in Jablanica?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Take into account your command position, did you know what had happened to the Croats in Jablanica, that they had been taken to the camp called Museum?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: What is the period that you are referring to?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Just before the conflict.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: That is not correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Are you trying to say that the camp at the museum did not exist at that time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: No, not while I was free, while I was still in that area.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Very well. Did you hear about places called Orliste and Trusina?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: You do not know what took place there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] For the record, the spelling for the two places is: Orliste is O-R-L-I-S-T-E. The other one is T-R-U-S-I-N-A.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: These places are not in the territory of Jablanica municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: A moment ago you said that you did not hear of those places?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: The reason is that I was born there, I lived there, and I know that such places -- such place names do not exist in the municipality of Jablanica.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: These places are in the Jablanica municipality, and you cannot really say anything about it if you don't know about it, if you are not aware that some of the major crimes against Croats occurred there on the eve of the 17th. And if you had not heard about it, you must have been informed about some of the events through the briefings at the brigade level?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. I will give the floor to Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes. Excuse me, Your Honour, but there seems to someone in here with a mobile phone which is allowed -- disallowed in the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Is there anyone with a mobile phone?

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My apologies. I was unable to get to it to turn it off. Can I please be allowed to leave the courtroom and deal with this?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, you will have to do that. It is not allowed to use a mobile phone in this courtroom. Yes, Mr. Stringer.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Mr. President, I had an objection to the last statement of Defence counsel beginning at line 22 of page 72, which is not a question at all but is rather simply a statement and is something which I think is not a proper statement to make to a witness who has already testified he doesn't know about things that may have happened elsewhere. So I object to the statement and I would ask that the Court order that it be stricken or that counsel not continue to make statements of that nature.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, we share the view expressed by the Prosecutors on this issue. It is really not a question; just a statement. So this paragraph will be stricken.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, with all due respect, I'm sorry that my explanation, if, that is, you allow me to do it, the witness will hear. And but if I may, I would like to take the liberty to make a very brief explanation; namely, for this Honourable Court to understand, to really get into the matter, into the events there, since my learned friend did not bother to provide a broader explanation of things which preceded some other events, and to my surprise, I always think that the Prosecutors need be objective. That is, before this Court, if not before their domestic courts. The Defence is exerting itself to present to this Court all the relevant facts about events which took place at that time, at that -- if I may call it that, that micro site. Because without it, the truth will never come to light.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: You have to bear in mind, that the alleged wrongdoings of the other side is not a proper Defence for your client before this Tribunal. You may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Tell me, please, and I am going back to Obruc now, you said that members of the 114th and 115th Split Brigade were there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: How do you know at what? Did it say so on their uniforms or did somebody else tell you or did you find that out later?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: Yes, they had it on their emblems. It said 114th Split Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Was it a Split Brigade or did it just say so, that? So they had emblems on the uniforms which said that. Is that what you are saying to say?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Tell me, now, please, how did you communicate from your command post with soldiers in Sovici and how did you communicate with your superior command in Jablanica?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: I had a portable radio of a rather old age, and I used it to communicate with the command in Jablanica, then I had four Motorolas and I used them to communicate with the guards at Brdo.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And you had no telephones?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: No, we did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Motorolas, didn't you have Motorolas to communicate with the command?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: We didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And about the soldiers on the positions, you used Motorolas to communicate with them, is that it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And you received reports about what went on in individual areas where the AbiH had the positions; you were kept abreast of all the events there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: I was.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Will you please be so kind as to tell me how many soldiers were there on the positions that morning?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: You mean all the positions or one by one?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Altogether, how many of them were there altogether, out on positions, and then we can perhaps specify Gruda and others.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: About six or seven men at each one of those positions.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: You mean at Borovnik, at Gruda -- no, sorry, Mackovic, Gruda, and Povrsak, that they were six men to a trench each in each direction, in each shift there were six or seven men, so three shifts of 24 men?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: There were no three shifts; one shift lasted 24 hours. I changed them every 24 hours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: I see. But in case of a conflict, had the Serbs come or -- how would you then organise them? Would everybody be at the position?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
