utterances.text: Well, then, more or less everybody who was available at the time would naturally undertake a defence mission.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And what do you mean "available"? What else can a soldier do in case of an attack? Would he have a day off on the day of attack?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: Well, if he has come back from a shift, then he should have a day off. But if there was an attack, then he wouldn't have a day off. He wouldn't be free.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: That's what I'm asking you, because if there is an attack, then there are no more days off. Everybody has to be on positions.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: Why, naturally.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Thank you. I mean, you know, I have to ask you that. You have to tell me that. I cannot draw any conclusions myself. So how many men were under arms at that time altogether?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: In Sovici, as a whole, about 85 men.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: You mean in the place, and what about the front lines?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: Well, in those three places, say -- I would say seven, so in three places, seven men each, so it would make 21.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And these 80 from Sovici, they didn't go over to help out up there because Jesic was up there, if I understood you well.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: Well, they couldn't come out, they couldn't get out because if Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. they were to approach those hills, it was a clearing, so there was no way in which you could approach them except get killed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And what did you do then with 80 men under arms in Sovici? Did they wait or what did they do?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: Well, they hid, I guess.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: They hid?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: They were under arms and they hid?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And those 21 men managed to withstand this attack for 10 or 12 hours?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: Well, I suppose they couldn't get through. Yes, they could, but they didn't.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could please the counsel and the witness not speak at the same time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Krsnik, did you hear the interpreter? She is asking you that both the Defence counsel and the witness do not speak at the same time. You really give a hard time to the interpreters.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Tell me, once you were at Obruc, did people talk to you nicely, no problems or anything?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: No, no, they did not cause any problems.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And they told you to take your family and go to Jablanica, is that it, in that van?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: Yes, they told me that nobody else could board that van apart from my family, that I should drive it, and that women, children should take the bus and be on their way to Jablanica.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: In a statement, you said that there were 30 people in that van.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: How big is that van? Is this a lorry or a bus or what?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: It's a van, I think eight plus one seats --

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Eight plus one seats, nevertheless 30 people managed to fit in and you left with them, towards Jablanica?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: Yes. When I told those who were there to board that van, my family and I, they all wanted to board that same van. That's why I'm saying there couldn't have been less than 30 people there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Did you have any problems talking people into surrendering, were people ready to surrender?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: Yes, they were.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Weren't you accused of treason and surrender and at 5.00 and didn't you run into big trouble because of that because of the fighting had been stopped because you didn't continue fighting?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: Well, I had nobody to fight with because the soldiers were already capturing civilians and since Sovici is as it is --

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: No, no, no, I'm asking you about the inhabitants. I'm sorry, Witness, why you see we do have problems with the interpretation, so let us try to slow down, both you and I. I had to interrupt you because my question was did the soldiers and inhabitants of Sovici accuse you of treason, of betrayal, because you stopped fighting at 1700 and they all wanted to go on fighting?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: There were all sorts of stories, but to me, to me personally, nobody said anything, anything like that. I mean to my face.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Weren't you accused by Sovicians that you had struck a deal to take your family to Jablanica and leave them to their own devices, and that that was why you surrendered the village, not because you were weaker, because you had less power and would have failed anyway?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: I am not aware of such stories. I am saying I heard all sorts of things that I was responsible, and so on and so forth, yes. They accused me that I was allegedly responsible because I protected the Croats in Sovici because they never had any problems there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Well, you mean that Croats had some problems or somebody wanted to cause trouble since you wanted to protect them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: No, they didn't really have problems because they didn't want to go to a war. No, they didn't want to come with us. They didn't want to be with us, and they said that they could -- they could just sit peacefully, but that they should be left alone and nobody should force them to join the defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And tell me, wasn't the Croatian flag burned on Easter '94 in the village of Sovici?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: Could you repeat that question, please? I didn't get it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Wasn't the Croatian flag burned on Easter '93?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: That's not true.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Do you know that two military policemen from Sovici were killed five days before the conflict?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: That's not true.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: So Croats had absolutely no problems in Sovici, nobody laid a finger on them, nobody attacked them, is that it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: That's it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Very well. Tell me, please, who commanded Mijat Tomic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: Stipe Pole.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And his deputy?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Krsnik, if we come to the part that will identify the witness, we better go into the private session.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, by all means, Your Honour, except that I do not know what the answer will be. My question was, who is that man? But yes, I am mindful of that, as you can see.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. President, I apologise for the interruption. Could we please request that the last answer be redacted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Sure, sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Will you please be so kind as to tell me, the second road that you said passed by Junuzovici houses, is it that famous road of salvation, as it used to be called?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: No, the famous road of salvation went through Sovici.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Tell me, please, did AID use the -- did the lorry brigade use that route?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: You mean the road passing by the Junuzovici houses?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: Well, that road was mostly used by the HVO driving to Doljani and taking that other route.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: But in view of your position, are you aware of the robbing of those trucks by the BH army?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: That is not true that the BH army robbed those trucks on that road because we simply had no control over that road.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And the Croats were -- had absolutely freedom of movement around?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: 100 percent.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: I see. Tell me, please, you mentioned the name Robo. Could you describe him, please? Could you tell us what that man looks like?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: Well, let's see. He was shorter than I could be, 174/75 centimetres tall, nothing much. He was very loud, and he beat real hard. That is how you could tell him, tell that it was he.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: No, I'm asking you what he looked like, the colour of his hair or something else. You know how one describes a man. Did he have a beard or didn't he have a beard or something?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: No, he didn't have a beard. But I could not really look at him all that often because he would strike me every time I looked up so that I didn't dare look at him.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And after you moved to that bus, that is you said a shift, and then there was a shift and then you went on towards Ljubuski, were those soldiers, were they military police?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: I don't know. All I know is that when I came to, it wasn't the same soldiers who had come with us to Sovicka Vrata.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And to round off this story with Robo, can you describe him to me or can't you describe him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: Well, I couldn't really describe him 100 percent. I told you roughly.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Right, right. I must ask you, I think the question is very simple. If you cannot describe him, then you cannot describe him, then that's that.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: Well, I tried to do that as much as I could. I'm telling you that I never dared look at him because he kept beating me and I had to look down.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Oh, very well. Can you describe a man who you said was called Cikota?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: Yes, I could: black hair, short hair, black uniform, well-built guy.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And how tall, for instance?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: Well, 178, 179, about my height.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And did you hear that he got killed? We are talking about the same man, aren't we?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Where was he killed, what you heard?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: I think it was the 21st of April when those soldiers came to the Ljubuski camp to shoot us. They said themselves that he got -- that Tuta said deputy Cikota had got killed; they would slay us all. That was on the 21st.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: On the 21st of April?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: I see. Tell me, please, who was the commander at the Heliodrom?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: All I know is who was the police commander at Heliodrom.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Well, you mean the military police?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: Why, yes, that's who guarded us down there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Right. So who was the commander of the military police at Heliodrom?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: Ante Smiljanic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Very well. Now, Witness Y, in the three statements that you gave, in the first statement, you said that you saw Tuta only once when he arrived in an Audi 100. In your second statement, you said that he came -- that he had come twice, once in Audi 100, and another time that he was doing a round of the cells.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Very well. That second time that you say that he did a round of cells, you were in the solitary confinement without any lights?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And weren't you blinded by the light when the door was opened?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: No, because it is down in the passage, and you have to get to the -- had to come to the door and introduce myself.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: In your last statement of the 9th of December, '98, you said that Tuta was there twice, but that he never once visited prisoners, that he would never move far away from the administration building. That was your last -- third and last statement?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: That is not true. I never said that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: What do you mean it is not true? You never said that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: I never said that. I always said that he came twice, first that he did not visit me, and the second time that he did visit me whilst I was in the solitary confinement.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Now, how did it then happen to be in your statement? Did you read it? Did you sign it? Did you speak the truth?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: Yes, all that I signed was so, but I'm positive that I never said anything like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Witness Y, you signed the statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Stringer.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Counsel's jumping around between three statements, and my proposal would be for counsel to put one or all of the statements to the witness so that he has an opportunity to know which statement he is being cross-examined on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: That's a good idea. You have all those statements? Yes, you may show them to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is your last statement, and it is marked in yellow, what you said, and your signature. But you can go through the whole statement.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: Your Honours, I affirm that I never stated this.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: But did you sign the statement?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: I can't even see my signature here.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Yes, because the signature is on the original, which my learned friend has. But there is a certificate that you signed it. You can look at the end. Will you turn the last page, and doesn't it say, "I sign it with my own hand"?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: Once again, Your Honours, I affirm that I never said this. It does say so here, but I do not see a signature. I do not remember signing this -- such a statement. So could anyone please, if somebody has this statement with my signature, could I please see it?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, maybe that's a problem of the language. I want to know what is the language that is used in the original statement? Maybe Mr. Stringer could help me.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Mr. President, the original language of this statement is French. It was then translated into English, and from English then into the witness's own language. So the signatures will appear on the original French version, which I don't have in the courtroom at this time. And I apologise for that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: That makes things more complicated.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: If it would assist, I can stipulate on behalf of the Prosecutor that the statement which we are referring to, which is from December of 1998, is one in which appear the words in the English language "He never came to see the prisoners, but remained near the administration buildings." I can inform the Trial Chamber that that is the sentence which appears in the English language, which is the -- the English language version, which is the passage that counsel is referring to. But I don't know if that helps, but we can make that stipulation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, the problem is that we don't know whether the three copies with the different languages are consistent or not. I think that's the very issue.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I believe I could get the French version in the courtroom very quickly, if it would assist in clarifying the matter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, yes, you may. Mr. Krsnik, while the Prosecutor is getting the original documents, would you please skip this question at this moment and then come back.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, in the statement of the 29 April, you also said something about the shift change at Obruc and you were beaten in the mud or something like that. You remember that you gave that evidence to the Prosecutor, how you heard a voice which later on you identified as belonging to Tuta ordering them to stop it and to move on. And today, you said that he simply said, "Good, move on." What is true?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: I was lying in the mud, and they were beating me. And somebody said, "It's all right. We have to move on." And as I was picking myself up from that mud, I saw that this man was Tuta.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: You see, there's a big difference. In your statement you said, "I heard a man saying 'that's enough.' Let's move on. When I looked up, I saw that it was Tuta." That is your statement given on 29 April, '97? Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: Yes, yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Is that how it was?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: So what you said today is not -- it's all right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: You see, in Bosnian, it all depends on the translation. To me, it's the same. "Enough," it's enough, and "It's all right"; both means stop.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Witness, you will agree with me, we both were taught the same language, Serbo-Croatian or Croato-Serb; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And you will agree with me that it is not the same to say, "It is enough," and, "It is all right." I don't know how you would make that equation.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: When you say something, it's all right, that means that's fine. Or you say, "That's enough," that means that's enough. At least, to me, that's how it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Very well. The man whom you called -- named Tuta, you saw him briefly there at Sovici, you said it was in front of a building. Did he ever touch you, did he ever lay a finger on you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: No, not me.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Now, let me ask you about the prison in Ljubuski. Who was the commander there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: Prlic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Was this the military or civilian police?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: Military police.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And he was a military police commander?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: I guess a military police commander because people said that he was in charge there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Now, tell me about this Ante Smiljanic and about Prlic. I'm referring to the Smiljanic from Heliodrom and the military police there.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Did you see anyone else, apart from the military police, that was dealing with prisoners?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: I didn't quite understand the question, what did you mean by that?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Was the military police in charge of the prisoners?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Tell me, you identified the person whom you called Tuta.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: How old is he, do you think, from his appearance? How old is he?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: I believe that he is about 60 now.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And the -- his beard that he used to wear, was it kind of blond like mine?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: It was about 1 centimetre long.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: But was it a colour like mine?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: Yeah, kind of reddish.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Will you tell us the shape of his frames; was it a full circle, like completely round?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: Yes, thin arms and fully round.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Tell me, you said that he had a hat. How could you tell about the length of his hair?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: Under the hat, there was quite a bit of hair down under.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And what was the colour of his hair?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: It was also kind of blond.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: You mean like mine or even lighter?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: Well, around there. I don't know, maybe a little darker.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I have completed my cross-examination but I would ask that the original statement be provided, because it is a statement that he gave to the OTP. All statements were given in the same fashion, with a certification page at the back accompanying all these statements. So perhaps we can just have that last page, perhaps not even the whole statement, but just the last page with his signature on it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you have anything to say, Mr. Stringer?

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: No, Mr. President, not at this stage. When the statement arrives, we can distribute that and, depending on your direction, if you want to give counsel an additional opportunity to cross in respect of the French version, that's fine with us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, I think the only issue is the consistency of the three translations, so this Trial Chamber would like to ask you to furnish the three copies of those statements to the Chamber and to the Defence counsel, and when we evaluate all the evidence, we will take that into consideration.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. We will do that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Any cross-examination from the Defence counsel for Mr. Martinovic? Mr. Par.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Witness Y. My name is Zelimir Par. I am the co-counsel of Mr. Martinovic, and I will ask you some questions relating to the events which you described earlier today. And the first one has to do with your taking part in a group that went to the Health Centre. First off, do you know the name of the unit where you were brought there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Do you remember the person who took you from the Heliodrom to that location? Have you perhaps remembered his name?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: I don't know. He was tall, dark, and we were brought there first to Rondo in a TAM truck, and all of those who had been there before to work said that they were going to Stela's.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Could you tell me who those were who went to work there? Do you have the names of any of these detainees?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: Yes, I do have a number of those names. For instance, Hasib Lulic, Enes Kladusak, Helbet, a man called Helbet, Feriz Kovac, Ahmet Kovac.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: If you could just keep it slow so that everything can be entered in record.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: There were other men from the Lulic family. And I only went there once to work.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Do you know approximately what day that was; the season, the month?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: I wouldn't be able to recall exactly what date it was. As I mentioned several times, I was beaten a number of times, and I could not keep track of all that, but I believe that that was during the summer.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: You mentioned that you were beaten several times, but on that day, you were not beaten?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: No, no, no, I never said I was beaten up that day. But no, I was not beaten on that day.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: In the group that went to work with you, was there also a person whose nickname was Tsotsatiki? Did he leave the Heliodrom along with you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: No, as I said previously, when we were made to go behind that wall, they brought him. Apparently he was sneaking into apartments.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: I understand. He did not leave with you from the Heliodrom?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: No, he did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Have you ever heard of a unit which was named Vinko Skrobo?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: How about a unit whose name was Mrmak? How about the unit Benko Penavic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: How about a commander nicknamed Baja?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: At the time when you were leaving the Heliodrom and you were being driven by the soldiers, are you sure that none of these units were mentioned at that time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: No. But I remembered the person who led us there, but I forgot his name.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Very well. I'll take you back to the map that my learned friend had given you to look at so that we can pinpoint the location where you were.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to ask the usher to please give us, again, the Prosecutor Exhibit 14.5. And I have a fresh copy of it, actually. We should probably use the fresh copy so that we can put in markings.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Please, look at it again. It's a photograph that you were already shown today and which you also marked today. That is the location where you were brought. Let me ask you to start by putting a circle around the area where you spent that day, and then we'll move on from there, and mark it with "1."

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Now, today you mentioned some kind of a wall behind which you were when this incident with Tsotsa took place. Could you tell me exactly where this wall was? Can you draw it in this picture and mark it with number "2."

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: I cannot draw it, but it is behind the structure which I circled. It's behind it. And there was an entrance door leading down to a basement there.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Very well. We will try to find another photograph where perhaps we will be able to see it. Were there any trenches, were there any sand bags there? What did it look like in that area?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: Yes, there were trenches down here. Here, you see, over here, and here, and we were brought there.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Now, about these sand bags, where were they? Were they next to the trenches?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: Yeah, on top of these trenches. There were logs, and then they were on top of these logs.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Very well. Now, could you mark with number "2" locations where these trenches and sand bags were.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: And you said that you saw those bags in another place. Could you please mark that, also.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Very well. So, let's describe it a little bit. With number 2, you marked trenches and sand bags which were in front of -- how would you call this structure around which there is number 2?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: You mean this structure?

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: This here was the hospital. I don't know exactly what this was.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: How about the other structure where you placed number 2?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: I don't know what this structure was. I only know that this structure on top was the hospital.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: I'll show you another map that is a photograph, which is showing the same neighbourhood but from a different vantage point. Perhaps from Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. this photograph you will be able to see and then mark that location.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is Prosecutor's Exhibit 14.3, and I would like the assistance of the usher to place it on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Please review it well, try to orient yourself. See if you can find the area which we were looking at and disregard the numbers that are marked there.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: Again, you can't see that wall because this wall, it was a wall that separated that property from the adjoining property. And it was perhaps 80 centimetres high, and on top of that was kind of a metal fence.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: There's a reason why I kind of insist on this wall. We need to identify in which unit's zone of responsibility that place was, so this is why I am trying to use these photographs. Is it the closest to the photograph which is marked number 1?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: How many metres, let's say, that wall was from that structure, from that building?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: Two to three metres, not more than that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. On which side of the building? Is it on the side that we can see?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: Yes, on the near side.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Very well. You said, when you arrived there at that location --

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, we no longer need this photograph. You can remove it. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: So you arrived there and you were met there by some soldiers. Were you able to recognise any of the soldiers? Did you know any one of these soldiers personally?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: At that time, did you know to which unit that belonged?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: How were they dressed? In other words, were they -- did they have any insignia that you could notice?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: Now I cannot remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Now, the prisoner named Tsotsa, where did you see him for the first time, in which situation? Where were you in relation to him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: We were behind this wall, and they fired bullets above our heads, and then suddenly there was this -- there was these noises. Then they left us, turned to Tsotsa and started beating him. And one of them asked, "Where did you find him?" And he said, "I don't know. He's sneaking through apartments." And they went on beating him.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Let me stop you there. The beatings, did you personally see him being beaten by anyone or did you just hear that, were you behind a wall, personally?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: I did see it because the wall was behind the building, and we were between the building and the wall. And they brought him to that area from which we could see that he was being beaten.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Did you know this Tsotsa from before?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Do you know his full name?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: I don't know. We always called him "Tsotsa." He was a mechanic, worked for the Igrogradja [phoen] Company.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Later, did you ever talk with him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: So if I understood you correctly, they beat him because they had discovered him somewhere. What else did they say?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: No, they only said that they had found him somewhere and that he was sneaking around.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Was he a prisoner or a soldier? How was he dressed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: He was dressed in civilian clothes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Was anybody else beaten in addition to him or was he the only one beaten?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: He was the only one beaten.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Did you recognise any of the soldiers who beat him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Today, you gave evidence that after this event, two prisoners went to pick up a dead body on the Bulevar?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: And you said that this was a prisoner who was killed when trying to escape across the line. How did you find out about that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: This is what the person who was sending those people there, that he had tried to escape, and that he was killed in the attempt, and that he should be brought back.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Were you able to confirm that through anyone else later on?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: Only then, and also from those two who had brought the body back. They said that they had brought this body back.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: But it was only during that period, and in relation to that single event that you know about this man. Now, let me ask you this, do you know what the name of the killed person was? Did anybody mention his name?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Now, did you see when this body was brought, what happened to that body after those two had gone to collect it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: I don't know after they brought him. I don't know what happened to it. The two of them just said that he was -- that they had brought him back to Liska Street to be buried.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Is that the reason, so that he could be buried there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: So he could be buried there.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: The location where the body was brought from, did you know that was the line of separation between the Croats and Muslims?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: I know that the Bulevar was the separation line.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Do you know that UNPROFOR was in charge of collecting bodies there because they were the only ones who had free access to the Bulevar during that period?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: No, I did not know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Do you know whether there is information on who killed this person? In other words, from which side the fire had come that killed him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: I don't know anything about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: You personally, you never saw the body, you never saw the injuries which the body had?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Let me now take you to the Rondo. Because you also mentioned an incident that took place in front of a building at the Rondo, which supposedly was a command post of a unit. Can you describe this building for me; how many floors, what was around it, was there a coffee bar there, a restaurant or anything like that. If you --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: There were two buildings there. From the street leading to the Rondo, to the right, as you turned, one building is like this, and the other one is like that. We were told to sit down and look down in front of it, and then when Tsotsa came --

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: We will come to that. But how many floors first?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Was it a tall building, a low building?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: Fairly low. Three, four, up to five floors.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Next to it or nearby, was there another building?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: Yes, a similar one, but they were not one by the other. They were at different angles in relation to each other.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Just the number of floors, you said a minimum of three floors?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: Yes, a minimum of three.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Now, please, let us look at another map. This is Prosecutor's exhibit 15.1, but before I hand it to you, I have to tell you that there were some markings made by the Prosecutor, and they have been deleted. So I will first hand that redacted map to the Prosecution Bench to see whether they have any objections to it before the witness sees.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Maybe Madam Registrar has a clean copy. We could use a clean copy.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You see, Your Honour, these are identical maps, and on this copy, the Prosecutor had some markings. I did not want these markings to show, so I really -- I deleted it, whited them out. And my question is simply to find out whether the Prosecution has any objections to this redacted map. If not, we can distribute all the copies to the parties.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Stringer.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Mr. President, if we could just take a quick look at the map. I think there will not be an objection to it, but I would like to...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Sure, sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Mr. President, we have no objection to it. But it does bear a Prosecution exhibit number, which should probably change.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Later on, when this document is tendered into the evidence, we will change a different number for it. Yes, if you could at this moment.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This exhibit will be D2/9.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, I will now ask you, I see that you're good with maps. Could you please look at it carefully and find in it the location which you referred to as the Rondo and mark with a pen the building in front of which this incident with Tsotsa took place. If you can just take time, review it, and then when you are done, we'll have it placed on the ELMO. Can you first orient yourself there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: It's not easy to orient myself.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Can I perhaps help you? You see the Rondo in the middle. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Now, in relation to the Rondo, where approximately in relation to the Rondo was that building? And after you've marked it, we'll have it placed on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: If you can't orient yourself, just tell us. We'll help you.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: What I'm confused by is these two streets. There's one that went from up there, and the other one went along the avenue. This is what makes it problematic for me.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Very well. If you're confused, it's better that you don't mark it at all.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y
utterances.text: I thought that this was Zagrebiska Street and it should be between that street and this.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I see that it's 4.00. I have more questions but perhaps this is the best point to break at today and continue tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you. And this document should be D2/9 rather than D29, as announced by the Madam Registrar. And Witness, would you please bear in mind that you are still under the oath, so during this period, you are not to talk to anyone about your testimony, and do not let others talk to you about the Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. testimony. Thank you. We'll adjourn until 9.30 tomorrow morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Tuesday, the 9th day of October, 2001, at 9.30 a.m.
